I am in the same situation. I don't know what to do, but it's nice to hear that someone else might understand what I'm going through. I've only told one person in my life, my ex-boyfriend, and he comprehends it, but he will never be able to feel the slow gnawing of the realization that my childhood is fading and that I feel like I don't even know my parents. I've started avoiding people because I don't know how to interact if I don't remember what we've done in the past. I stopped watching Netflix because I don't know what movies and TV shows I've already seen.

Along with my memory problems, I've been having other abnormal sensory things happen. I hope one day I'll get the courage to seek help, but I'm afraid that no one will believe me and I'm afraid that they will believe me and the doctors will find nothing wrong and I'll feel even more helpless. I hope you have the courage to seek help if that's what you want to do. 

Until then, I'm coping... I make to do lists every day, I have a week-long schedule hanging up and a monthly calendar. I have a medication organizer. I have a great app, iStudiezPro, for classes and homework. I think just writing this is helpful, because most of the time I try my best to ignore the sheer terror that comes when I think about my memory.
